pr_title: apiextensions: fix items+type logic in API due to broken go-openapi validation
pr_body:
* Half of the fix (items without type) was done in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/76124.
* Second half (type:array without items) is done here.
* In addition this fixes 
* Finally we forgot to disable go-openapi meta checks for default validation.

Plus this PR add an integration test.

/kind bug

Fixes  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/84880

```release-note
CRDs can have fields named `type` with value `array` and nested array with `items` fields without validation to fall over this.
```

issue_context.title: Property names "items" in OpenAPISchema for CRD not handled correctly
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
 Created a CRD with OpenAPISchema containing an array which itself contains objects which have a property names "items". This already exists in [DownwardAPI volume source](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.16/#downwardapivolumesource-v1-core).

Creating a resource with this CRD fails with:
`The Foo "test" is invalid: type: Required value`

**What you expected to happen**:

It would succeed CRD validation.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:v1.16.2
Kubectl apply the following CRD:

```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: foos.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: foos
    singular: foo
    kind: Foo
  preserveUnknownFields: false
  validation:
    openAPIV3Schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        apiVersion:
          type: string
        kind:
          type: string
        metadata:
          type: object
        spec:
          type: object
          properties:
            volumes:
              type: array
              items:
                type: object
                properties:
                  downwardAPI:
                    properties:
                      items:
                        items:
                          properties:
                            path:
                              type: string
                          required:
                          - path
                          type: object
                        type: array
                    type: object
```

Then kubectl apply the following

```
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  volumes:
  - downwardAPI:
      items:
        - path: annotations
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):

```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.2", GitCommit:"c97fe5036ef3df2967d086711e6c0c405941e14b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T19:18:23Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.2", GitCommit:"c97fe5036ef3df2967d086711e6c0c405941e14b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-11-05T23:58:50Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
```

VERSION="18.3 (Sylvia)"
ID=linuxmint
ID_LIKE=ubuntu

VERSION_ID="18.3"
HOME_URL="http://www.linuxmint.com/"

```
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

This issue was meant to be fixed by https://github.com/go-openapi/validate/pull/107
However, there is a discussion: https://github.com/go-openapi/validate/issues/108#issuecomment-540532114

review_comments: do we need to turn these on when validating the schema itself? does this change to default these off loosen our validation on CRD's themselves (not the CRs)?
We don’t use meta validation of schemas using go-openapi.
this adds to the accepted formats the `datetime` validator permits, the docs added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/85381/files#r347187064 are not complete
we can easily override the time format, copy their regexps and that way stop adding ISO8601LocalTime.

The validation code path does not use the `ISO8601LocalTime` regex, but only the one for rfc3339. This means that the `datetime` format in our API rejects e.g. timezone-less `2006-01-02T15:04:05`, but also the mille and micro second variant. I don't know why the upstream project added that support to their unmarshaller.
With that, I think this PR is fine.
